enquiry: Our research group is evaluating a spectral measurement interface using model biological tissues such as chicken muscle, fat and liver. We want to compare MIR ATR and fluorescence information, because the material is heterogeneous and sequential measurements may not sample the same location. This is a laboratory classification study. We need a first comparison experiment and a clear statement of what its results would demonstrate.

clarification_questions.question: What decision should the classification result support, for example distinguishing tissue types in a lab workflow or a later sensor choice?
clarification_questions.why: Defines what the comparison must demonstrate and whether the study stays at lab scale.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Study is a lab-only method comparison; no sensor or application decision is implied.

clarification_questions.question: Which classes must be distinguished (muscle, fat, liver only, or further sub-states), and is there a required class-discrimination endpoint?
clarification_questions.why: Sets the classification task and the number of classes the comparison must separate.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Classes are the three named tissues; the endpoint is to be defined in lab screening.

clarification_questions.question: In what physical form and surface state are the tissue samples presented to the ATR crystal (fresh, frozen-thawed, sliced, homogenised), and how much do they vary within a tissue type?
clarification_questions.why: Determines contact quality, sample homogeneity and the sampling depth relevance for MIR-ATR.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Solid tissue with uncontrolled surface; contact and heterogeneity are treated as sources of variation to be tested.

clarification_questions.question: What fluorescence excitation and emission setup is planned, and which fluorescent species (intrinsic or added indicator) are expected in each tissue?
clarification_questions.why: Fluorescence only carries information for a defined fluorescent species; this decides whether the fluorescence arm is valid.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Fluorescent species unknown; lab screening first identifies whether any defined fluorophore gives class-relevant signal.

clarification_questions.question: Which hardware is available for the same-spot measurement (combi probe, separate ATR and fluorescence probes, fiber type and whether it transmits mid-IR), and is the spectrometer close to the sample?
clarification_questions.why: Decides whether MIR can be carried by the fiber and whether both methods can sample the same spot.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Hardware undefined; the design assumes a lab bench setup with both probes at one spot, and mid-IR fiber requirements are to be confirmed.

clarification_questions.question: How is the true tissue identity established for each sample (histology, dissection record, or other), and how accurate is it?
clarification_questions.why: Without a trusted reference, classification accuracy cannot be interpreted.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference is the known dissection origin; its accuracy is unverified.

clarification_questions.question: What sample numbers, independent batches or animal lots are available, and what classification accuracy or confusion level would count as a useful result?
clarification_questions.why: Sets how the results are validated on independent runs before any combination of methods is considered.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Sample set and acceptance criterion undefined; validation uses independent batches and single-method results are judged first.

not_supported: S01 p.5 only says fluorimetry is based on emission of certain, mostly biological, substances. It does not say that fluorescence measures only a defined fluorescent species, and it says nothing about the species in each tissue being unidentified. Fix: State only that fluorescence responds to certain fluorescent (mostly biological) substances, and drop the claim about unidentified species unless a source supports it.

not_supported: The cited page S04 p.3 reports a fluorescence band with maximum at 520-530 nm (FAD). It does not mention a 613 nm peak or fluorescence recognising liver. The 613 nm detail appears only on the uncited S02 p.15 slide. Fix: Cite S02 p.15 and S04 p.4 for the liver recognition and the 613 nm wavelength, or remove the 613 nm detail and say fluorescence was better suited to liver tissue per S04 p.4.

not_supported: S04 p.3 attributes low reproducibility of fat samples to tissue inhomogeneity. It does not mention contact quality, nor say that contact or heterogeneity can mimic class differences. Fix: Restrict the risk to heterogeneity causing poor reproducibility (as in S04 p.3), and cite a source for contact quality or remove that element.

RAMAN.nominal_range: Raman shift in cm-1; signal recorded in the visible / short-wave NIR (400-1100 nm); state the laser excitation separately [S01 p.11]

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]

fiber_limits_wavelength: The fiber determines which wavelengths reach the probe. Silica fibers transmit up to about 2.4 um and cannot carry mid-IR; mid-IR needs chalcogenide, polycrystalline or hollow-waveguide fibers. [S02 p.6; S04 p.1; DOCX §5]
remote_measurement_nir_silica: NIR works with standard glass optics and silica fibers, which suits remote online measurement; robust silica cables of 100-300 m exist. [S01 p.5; S02 p.7]
same_spot_for_heterogeneous: For heterogeneous or fast-changing samples, methods should measure the same spot at the same time, e.g. with a combi probe. [S01 p.8; S04 p.2]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
